# ingest-corrupts-post-body-text — analysis (generated by analyst on 2026-08-06)

## Problem

`post.body` is stored in a representation that is neither the publisher's
text nor plain text: allowlisted markup (`<p>`, `<a href>`) stands, and six
ASCII punctuation characters are rewritten as numeric HTML entities. The
column is not display-only — the tagger, classifier, entity extractor,
body-summarizer, ingest translator and the embedding vector all read it, and
`post.search_tsv` is a GENERATED column over it — so the corruption degrades
every LLM verdict and the lexical arm of D58 hybrid retrieval, not only what
a reader sees.

Observed on the v1.1.0 live run (`.scratch/V1.1.0-TEST-REPORT-CLEAN-RUN.md`
§F1, lines 84–98): a `/saved` line rendered

```
<p>V každém projektu, ke kterému se připojím, slyším stejnou větu…
https://www.web3isgoinggreat.com/?id&#61;coldcard-hardware-wallet-flaw
```

The evidence file's own measurement is **142/353 = 40 %** of posts ready in
a 3-hour window carrying `&#NN;` entities (rss 136/334, nitter 5/18,
odysee 1/1), and "Stored `body` samples contain `<p>`, `<a href="…"
rel="nofollow">`, `</p>`. `title`/`url` are clean."

Reproduction: `app.zcat.infochat.collector.eval.stage1.Stage1BodyTextIT`,
11 cases, 8 failing on unmodified `main`, 0 errors.

## Ground truth

### The pipeline, as it exists

`Stage1Pipeline.process`
(`infochat-collector/src/main/java/app/zcat/infochat/collector/eval/stage1/Stage1Pipeline.java:266`–`286`)
runs, in order:

1. `StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4(safeBody)` — **one** pass (`:273`).
2. `unicodeNormalize` = NFKC + `IngestTextNormalizer.stripBidiAndZeroWidth`
   (`:274`, `:297`–`306`; the strip loop is
   `infochat-core/src/main/java/app/zcat/infochat/core/ingest/IngestTextNormalizer.java:54`–`79`).
   The result is the local `normalized`.
3. `findAllMatchesUnderWatchdog(normalized)` (`:277`) — the seven
   `Stage1RegexSet` rules, offsets indexing `normalized`.
4. Redaction of the matched spans **in `normalized`** (`:398`–`408`), one
   `quarantine` row per match.
5. `safeSanitize(...)` → `sanitize(input)` → `OWASP_POLICY.sanitize(input)`
   (`:390` clean path, `:422` match path, `:523`–`544`).
6. `updatePostBodyAndFlags` writes that string to `post.body` (`:427`,
   `:587`–`599`).

`OWASP_POLICY` is `Sanitizers.FORMATTING.and(BLOCKS).and(LINKS)` (`:225`–`228`);
the library is `com.googlecode.owasp-java-html-sanitizer:20240325.1`
(`infochat-collector/pom.xml:128`–`130`).

**The store is therefore step 5's output, and the scan is step 3's input.
They are different strings.** That single fact is the root of both defect
groups.

### What produces the corruption

Step 5 is an *HTML sanitizer*, not a text extractor: it re-serializes
allowlisted markup and escapes HTML-significant characters. The reproduction's
own failure output is the direct proof, and it needs no external claim:

- `htmlMarkupDoesNotReachTheBodyColumn` read back
  `<p>Hello <a href="https://x.test" rel="nofollow">link</a></p>` — tags
  survive, and the sanitizer even *adds* `rel="nofollow"`.
- `plainTextPunctuationPersistsVerbatim` seeded `We're working on it!!` —
  **no markup at all** — and read back `We&#39;re working on it!!`.
- `urlQueryStringPersistsAsAWorkingUrl` read back `?id&#61;coldcard-…`.

The second case is decisive by elimination: between the seeded string and the
column there are exactly three transforms — `unescapeHtml4` (decodes only),
NFKC + codepoint strip (cannot emit `&#39;`), and `OWASP_POLICY.sanitize`. The
encoding is ours. The brief's per-fetcher table (bluesky: 248 posts, 0 raw
HTML upstream, 101 with entities) corroborates it from live data; that table
is a live-DB query I could not re-run, so it is recorded here as
**corroboration, not as a verified count** — the verified proof is the
reproduction above. The evidence file's own 3-hour histogram (40 %,
rss/nitter/odysee only, no bluesky row in that window) is what
`.scratch/V1.1.0-TEST-REPORT-CLEAN-RUN.md:94`–`95` states, and it differs from
the brief's 8-hour table; neither number changes any conclusion here.

The six characters in the brief's histogram (`= ' " @ + \``) are exactly the
non-`&<>` members of the sanitizer's escape set, which is why they and only
they appear.

### The design tier already required the fix

`docs/design/04-security.md:94`–`97`, §4.2 step 4:

> 4. **Parse with OWASP Java HTML Sanitizer** on the placeholder-redacted body.
>    - Allowlist: `p, br, a (href only, http/https), strong, em, ul, ol, li, code, pre, blockquote, h1-h6`
>    - Strip everything else (script, style, iframe, object, form, on*, javascript:, data:, file:, etc.)
>    - **Convert allowed-but-formatted HTML to plain text equivalent for storage in `post.body`**

Bullet 3 was never implemented. `docs/spec/security.md:137`–`170` (§Ingest
pipeline) says only "HTML is sanitized against an allowlist" and is silent on
the stored representation, so **there is no spec gap**: the change conforms the
implementation to a design-tier requirement, under a spec that does not
contradict it, on a surface D30 already governs (plain-text output).

`RssFeedParser` states the same division of labour from the other side
(`infochat-collector/src/main/java/app/zcat/infochat/collector/fetcher/rss/RssFeedParser.java:33`,
`:44`–`49`): "body ← `<description>` (raw HTML preserved) … HTML stripping,
NFKC normalization, and redaction live at Stage 1 downstream … NOT here."
`PostPersister` binds the body verbatim (`PostPersister.java:188`) while the
title and url *are* stripped (`:187`, `:177`) — which is why the evidence file
found `title`/`url` clean and only `body` dirty.

### Who reads the corrupted column

- Collector: `TaggerWorker`, `ClassifierWorker`, `EntityExtractorWorker`,
  `BodySummaryWorker`, `EmbeddingWorker`, `IngestTranslationWorker` (all read
  `body` in their pickup SQL).
- `post.search_tsv` is `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('english',
  coalesce(title_en, title, '') || ' ' || coalesce(body_en, body, '')))`
  (`infochat-core/src/main/resources/db/migration/V74__post_english_anchor.sql:58`–`63`)
  — the lexical arm of `semanticSearch`.
- Provider: `DisplayHeadline` falls back to `post.body` whenever the title is
  blank or equals `IngestTextNormalizer.UNTITLED_TITLE`
  (`infochat-provider/src/main/java/app/zcat/infochat/provider/render/DisplayHeadline.java:162`–`171`,
  `:183`) — which is exactly how a titleless post rendered `<p>V každém…` in
  `/saved`.
- `SaveCommandHandler` **snapshots** `post.body` into `saved_post.body`
  (`SaveCommandHandler.java:143`–`146`, `:375`), per schema.md §Posts and
  derivatives / Invariant 6 (snapshot so partition drops do not break the
  bookmark). Corrupted text therefore leaves permanent per-user copies that no
  post-retention partition drop ever reaches.

Writers of `post.body` are exactly three: `PostPersister` (INSERT, verbatim),
`Stage1Pipeline` (UPDATE), and `approve_quarantine`'s placeholder restore.

### The scan/store mismatch is exploitable **today** — the brief understates it

The brief records Group B as latent ("something downstream of the scan is
incidentally neutralizing payloads"). Verification says: that is true for the
two payloads the reproduction happens to use, and **false in general**.

The neutralizer is the sanitizer's *re-encoding*. It only neutralizes payloads
whose decisive character is inside its escape set (`` ` `` and `<`/`>` — the
reproduction's two cases). A payload whose decisive characters are outside it
is decoded by step 5's HTML parse and stored **decoded and unflagged**:

```
raw       &amp;#105;gnore previous instructions
step 1    &#105;gnore previous instructions        (unescapeHtml4 is a single pass)
step 3    no rule matches — there is no "ignore" substring
step 5    the HTML parse decodes &#105; → 'i'; letters are not re-escaped
stored    "ignore previous instructions", stage1_flagged = FALSE, 0 quarantine rows
```

That is redteam M1-032 Finding 1 — the vector the pre-decode at `:273` exists
to close, quoted in the class javadoc at `:34`–`48` — reopened by adding one
encoding layer. Same shape for rule 3 via `&amp;#58;` (`:`) and rule 7 via
`&amp;#40;` (`(`); none of those characters is in the escape set. I did not
run this case (no build in this session); it is derived from the code path
above and from the reproduction's own evidence that the identical single-encoded
form is caught (`Stage1PipelineIT` @Order(9)–(11), `:311`–`370`) while the
sanitizer decodes what the regex did not see.

### The four Group B cases, traced

| case | scan sees | store gets, today | after a plain-text fix, without a rescan |
|---|---|---|---|
| doubly-encoded backticks | `&#96;&#96;&#96;system` — no match | `&#96;…` re-encoded, inert | `` ```system `` **literal, unflagged** |
| normalization-synthesized `&lt;` | `&lt;system&gt;` — no match (the ZWSP made the entity invalid until *after* the pre-decode) | `&lt;…` re-encoded, inert | `<system>` **literal, unflagged** |
| block-close line start | one line — `(?m)^` cannot reach `system:` (`Stage1RegexSet.java:117`–`121`) | one line, inert | `Weekly roundup.\nsystem: …` **line-anchored payload, unflagged** |
| inline-tag-split backtick run | `` `<b>``</b>system `` — not contiguous | split, inert | `` ```system `` **joined, unflagged** |

So the display fix, shipped alone, converts four inert cases into four live
ones. That is the central coupling of this problem.

### Controls that already exist on this path

- `quarantine` restore is **placeholder-keyed, not offset-keyed**:
  `UPDATE post SET body = replace(body, '[REDACTED:' || v_placeholder_id || ']', v_original_html)`
  (`infochat-core/src/main/resources/db/migration/V69__approve_quarantine_verdict_owed_guard.sql:150`).
  A second scan may therefore record spans indexing a different string without
  breaking the restore — but a redaction that *overwrites part of* a
  placeholder makes the restore a silent no-op.
- The placeholder is 37 chars (`[REDACTED:` + 26 base32 + `]`, pinned by
  `Stage1BodyTextIT.PLACEHOLDER_SHAPE:86`–`87`; `docs/design/04-security.md:91`),
  and rules 1/2/4 carry `.{0,40}` DOTALL interstitials
  (`Stage1RegexSet.java:99`–`132`) — wide enough to straddle one.
- Fail-closed: `security.md:1406`–`1410` — "Stage 1 infrastructure failure
  (regex watchdog crash, HTML sanitizer exception) → fail-closed". The seam is
  the package-private `Stage1Pipeline.sanitize` (`:542`), deliberately
  overridable, and `Stage1PipelineIT.SanitizerThrowingStage1Pipeline`
  (`:629`–`641`) is the only way the branch is reached (@Order(12)/(13),
  `:372`–`446`).
- Budgets: `infochat.security.stage1.regex-timeout-ms=100` and
  `infochat.security.stage1.max-matches=1000`
  (`infochat-collector/src/main/resources/application.properties:379`, `:397`).
  The spec commits to a **per-input** wall-clock watchdog
  (`security.md:145`–`150`); the deadline is currently computed inside
  `findAllMatchesUnderWatchdog` (`:330`).

## Root cause

Two causes, one structural invariant.

**Cause 1 — the output sink is a serializer, not an extractor.** Stage 1's
final step re-renders the allowlisted parse tree as HTML. Design §4.2 step 4
bullet 3 requires the opposite (plain-text equivalent). The escape set and the
surviving tags are properties of that sink alone; nothing upstream introduces
them.

**Cause 2 — Stage 1 scans a string it does not store.** The regex set runs on
`normalized` (`:277`) and the column receives `sanitize(redacted)` (`:427`).
Every transformation between those two points is outside the scan: entity
decoding by the HTML parse (live today), and — once Cause 1 is fixed —
newline synthesis at block close, text-run joining by tag removal, and
verbatim entity decoding.

The invariant that covers both, and the one the fix should be derived from:

> **The text Stage 1 writes to `post.body` must be a text Stage 1 scanned.**

Note what this invariant deliberately does *not* claim: it does not promise to
defeat arbitrary encoding depth. `docs/design/04-security.md:103` already
disclaims that — "multilingual, paraphrased, base64-encoded, and otherwise
obfuscated injection bypasses Stage 1 by design". A triply-encoded payload that
Stage 1 stores still-encoded stores something *inert*, and that is in-policy.
What is out of policy is Stage 1 **itself decoding or restructuring** a payload
after the scan and then storing the result.

## Pitfalls

- **P1 — Giving the second scan its own watchdog deadline and its own match
  cap.** `findAllMatchesUnderWatchdog` computes `deadlineNanos` internally
  (`Stage1Pipeline.java:330`) and caps against `maxMatches` per call
  (`:337`). A second call silently doubles both. `security.md:145`–`150` commits
  to a **per-input** wall-clock cap; doubling the CPU an attacker-chosen body
  can command is trading away a stated bound (engineering-rules §2). The
  deadline and the remaining match budget must be hoisted to `process()` and
  shared.
- **P2 — A second-pass redaction that overlaps a first-pass placeholder.**
  `approve_quarantine` restores with a literal
  `replace(body, '[REDACTED:'||id||']', original)`
  (`V69…sql:150`). Overwrite one byte of a 37-char marker and the restore
  becomes a silent no-op: the quarantine row can never be lifted and the
  pipeline's own stated consistency property ("post.body's placeholders match
  quarantine rows", `Stage1Pipeline.java:420`–`421`, `:443`–`447`) is broken with
  no failing test. Reachable, not theoretical: rules 1/2/4 allow `.{0,40}`
  DOTALL between anchors and the marker is 37 chars.
- **P3 — "Just scan after the transformation" (drop the pre-parse scan).** An
  HTML parse *drops comments entirely* and mangles `<<<UNTRUSTED>>>`, so
  rule 5 (`<!--.*?-->`, `Stage1RegexSet.java:134`–`136`) could never fire again
  and rule 6's `<<<UNTRUSTED>>>` alternative (`:139`–`146`) would lose the shape
  it is designed to catch — the exact reason the class javadoc calls the step
  order load-bearing (`Stage1Pipeline.java:91`–`115`) and the reason
  `Stage1PipelineIT` @Order(8) exists. Stage 1 is required to *record and route
  to review* (`security.md:169`–`170`), so losing the quarantine row is a
  control loss even where the payload is removed from the body anyway.
- **P4 — A plain-text sink that collapses or re-normalizes whitespace.** HTML
  rendering collapses runs of whitespace; ingest must not. Bluesky and Nostr
  bodies are plain text with real newlines and no markup at all, so collapsing
  would (a) break byte-identical persistence and (b) destroy pre-existing line
  starts that rule 3's `(?m)^` anchors on — removing detection while claiming
  to add it.
- **P5 — Losing the `script`/`style` element-CONTENT drop when the sink is
  swapped.** That drop is a property of the current output path, and the
  pre-existing `Stage1PipelineIT` @Order(7) (`:259`–`280`) only asserts the
  absence of the literal `<script` and `javascript:` — it stays green while
  `alert(1)` leaks into the column as text. Engineering-rules §10: the
  replaced path's incidental controls do not travel with its stated purpose.
- **P6 — Losing the sanitizer-exception fail-closed branch.** The
  `RuntimeException → SanitizerFailedException → handleSanitizerException →
  status='QUARANTINED'` route (`Stage1Pipeline.java:523`–`529`, `:557`–`585`) is
  spec-committed (`security.md:1406`–`1410`) and is reachable in tests only
  through the package-private `sanitize` seam that
  `Stage1PipelineIT.SanitizerThrowingStage1Pipeline` overrides (`:629`–`641`).
  A new output method that bypasses the seam silently deletes both the control
  and the two tests that pin it.
- **P7 — `[REDACTED:<id>]` not surviving the new sink byte-exact.** The marker
  is a spec-level commitment (`security.md:158`–`168`,
  `security.md:1374`–`1378`) and `/quarantine approve` matches it literally.
- **P8 — `Stage1Result.redactedBody` diverging from what was written.** Its
  contract is "what `post.body` now holds in the DB"
  (`Stage1Pipeline.java:714`–`717`). A second-pass redaction applied to the DB
  string but not to the record makes the hand-off carrier lie to Stage 2 and to
  every test that reads it instead of the column.
- **P9 — Shipping the representation fix without the rescan.** The four Group B
  cases above show the plain-text conversion *manufacturing* payloads: a
  newline at a block close puts `system:` at a line start; removing an inline
  tag joins `` ` `` + ` `` ` into ` ``` `; the parse decodes `&#96;`/`&lt;`. Each
  lands in `post.body` unflagged and unquarantined. A display fix that weakens
  a stated security control is engineering-rules §2 and §6 — escalate, never
  pick which to violate.
- **P10 — "Decode to a fixpoint" as the cure for the encoding half.** It looks
  like the obvious fix and is wrong twice: it corrupts legitimately-escaped
  prose (a post *about* HTML that writes `&amp;lt;` would store `<`), and it
  chases exactly the obfuscation depth `docs/design/04-security.md:103`
  declines to chase. The invariant is "scan what you store", not "decode
  everything".
- **P11 — Remediating stored rows with SQL or a hand-rolled regex.** That is a
  second, drifting decoder that will disagree with the pipeline's parser on the
  first malformed tag, and it rewrites already-scanned text *without* rescanning
  it — reintroducing Cause 2 on the remediation path.
- **P12 — Remediating `post.body` and forgetting `saved_post.body`.** `/saved`
  — the surface the defect was actually observed on — renders the snapshot
  (`SaveCommandHandler.java:143`–`146`, `:375`), and snapshots are permanent by
  design (schema.md §Posts and derivatives, Invariant 6): partition retention
  never reaches them.
- **P13 — Committing the reproduction file's prose unchanged.** Its javadoc
  cites `docs/plan/m1/redteam/M1-776-2026-08-06.md`, absent from `main`, and
  asserts an implementation shape as fact. The assertions are the contract; the
  prose must describe what is built.
- **P14 — Converting a stored row twice.** The conversion is safe exactly once.
  An old-pipeline row cannot contain a raw `<` that is not a real tag, because
  the serializer escaped every literal one; after conversion it can (a post
  about HTML now legitimately reads `use <b> for bold`), and a second pass would
  strip it. At-most-once per row has to be a property of the schema, not of the
  operator remembering — which is why the remediation ticket carries a marker
  column and `migration_touch: true`.

## Solution options

**Option A — Replace the output sink, keep the policy (CHOSEN for the
representation half).** `OWASP_POLICY` still decides which elements and
attributes survive; only the *emitter* changes, from the library's HTML
renderer to a text sink that appends element text and a `\n` at block
boundaries. Spec refs: `docs/design/04-security.md §4.2` step 4 bullet 3
(literally this), `docs/spec/security.md §Ingest pipeline` (allowlist
sanitization unchanged), D30. Cost/risk: the script/style content drop and the
fail-closed seam must be re-proven, not assumed (P5, P6). Smallest change that
satisfies bullet 3: the allowlist, the scheme filter and the `on*` strip are
untouched because the policy is untouched.

**Option B — Add jsoup and use `Jsoup.parse(html).text()`.** Rejected: a second
HTML parser alongside the one that makes the allowlist decision is a
parser-differential bug waiting to happen, and `docs/design/04-security.md:94`
names the OWASP sanitizer at design tier, so swapping libraries is a
design-note amendment for no gain.

**Option C — Hand-roll a tag-stripping pass.** Rejected: reimplementing HTML
tokenization, and it would disagree with the policy about what is markup.

**Option D — Move the HTML step before the regex set and scan once.**
Rejected on P3: it deletes rule 5 detection outright and blinds rule 6's
`<<<UNTRUSTED>>>` alternative. The step-order commitment
(`Stage1Pipeline.java:91`–`115`, `docs/design/04-security.md:62`) exists for
this reason.

**Option E — Decode entities to a fixpoint before the scan.** Rejected on P10.

**Option F — Constrain the plain-text step so it cannot synthesize
structure.** Not viable: the reproduction *requires* the synthesis
(`<p>one</p><p>two</p>` → `one\ntwo`), and removing tags necessarily joins the
runs they separated.

**Option G — Scan the final string as well (CHOSEN for the mismatch half).**
Keep the existing pre-parse scan exactly as it is (so no current detection or
test moves) and add a second scan over the exact string about to be written,
sharing one deadline and one match budget, redacting its matches and writing
their quarantine rows, skipping any match that overlaps an existing
placeholder. Spec refs: `docs/spec/security.md §Ingest pipeline` (the regex set
runs on the body; matches are recorded as quarantine spans and replaced by the
marker), `§Failure handling` (fail-closed unchanged), `§Quarantine workflow`.
Cost/risk: P1, P2, P8. Independently valuable *before* the representation
change, because it closes the live double-encoding bypass.

## Chosen approach

Option G first, then Option A, then remediation.

**Order, and why.** G before A is not cosmetic. G makes the pipeline
*transformation-agnostic*: once "Stage 1 scans the string it stores" holds, A
changes only what that string is, and the two Group B synthesis cases (block
close, joined runs) go green in A with **no additional scanning machinery** —
the guard is already there. The reverse order requires A to introduce both the
transformation and its guard in one diff, which is the shape that historically
costs three redteam rounds on this surface. G is also independently shippable
and independently valuable: it closes the `&amp;#105;gnore` bypass today.

**Decision → spec ref, per decision:**

| decision | spec ref |
|---|---|
| Stage 1's stored body is plain text | `docs/design/04-security.md §4.2` step 4 bullet 3 (line 97) |
| The allowlist, scheme filter and `on*` strip are unchanged | `docs/spec/security.md §Ingest pipeline`; `docs/design/04-security.md §4.2` step 4 bullets 1–2 |
| Every match is recorded as a quarantine span and replaced by `[REDACTED:<id>]`, including second-pass matches | `docs/spec/security.md §Ingest pipeline` (lines 156–168) |
| One per-input wall-clock cap across both scans | `docs/spec/security.md §Ingest pipeline` (lines 145–150) |
| Watchdog / overflow / sanitizer-exception stay fail-closed to `QUARANTINED` | `docs/spec/security.md §Failure handling` (lines 1406–1410) |
| The marker stays byte-exact so `/quarantine approve` restores | `docs/spec/security.md §Quarantine workflow` (lines 1374–1378) |
| Stage 2 keeps seeing the pre-redaction original | `docs/spec/security.md §Ingest pipeline` (line 171) |
| Stage 1 is not required to defeat arbitrary encoding depth | `docs/design/04-security.md §4.2` (line 103) |
| Snapshots are remediated alongside posts | `docs/spec/schema.md §Posts and derivatives` (Invariant 6, D13) |

**Files to touch (whole programme).** `Stage1Pipeline.java`; one new
package-private text-sink class beside it; `Stage1PipelineIT.java` (added
methods, no existing method modified); `Stage1BodyTextIT.java` (the
reproduction); `docs/design/04-security.md` §4.2 (the "Unicode-first,
OWASP-last" rationale paragraph, whose stated reason — the renderer's
entity-encoding — no longer applies once the renderer is gone, while the
ordering itself still holds for P3's reason). Remediation adds one Flyway
migration, one Collector job class and its IT.

## Controls to preserve (engineering-rules §10)

The path being re-parameterized is "Stage 1's output sink and the scan that
covers it". Its incidental obligations:

| control | where it lives today | how it is carried |
|---|---|---|
| Allowlist strip of `script`/`style`/`iframe`/`object`/`form` and every `on*` attribute | `Stage1Pipeline.java:225`–`228` (policy) | policy object untouched; only the emitter changes |
| `script`/`style` **element content** dropped, not just the tag | property of the current output path; only weakly pinned by `Stage1PipelineIT` @Order(7) `:259`–`280` | re-proven by `Stage1BodyTextIT.scriptAndStyleElementContentIsStillDropped` (passes on `main` today — it must still pass) |
| `javascript:` / `data:` / `file:` schemes never reach the column | `Sanitizers.LINKS` URL filter | `Stage1BodyTextIT.eventHandlersAndDangerousSchemesNeverReachTheBodyColumn` (passes today) |
| `[REDACTED:<id>]` byte-exact so `approve_quarantine`'s literal `replace` matches | `V69…sql:150`; `Stage1Pipeline.java:402`–`403` | `Stage1BodyTextIT.redactionPlaceholderSurvivesByteExact` (passes today) + P2's overlap rule |
| Sanitizer-exception → fail-closed `QUARANTINED` + one whole-body row | `Stage1Pipeline.java:523`–`529`, `:557`–`585` | the package-private `sanitize` seam stays; `Stage1PipelineIT` @Order(12)/(13) unchanged |
| Watchdog and match-overflow fail-closed branches | `:449`–`506` | unchanged; both scans feed the same two exceptions |
| Entity pre-decode (M1-032 Finding 1) | `:273` | unchanged; `Stage1PipelineIT` @Order(9)–(11) unchanged |
| Delimiter/comment detection on the pre-parse form | `Stage1RegexSet.java:134`–`146`; `Stage1PipelineIT` @Order(8) | the first scan is not moved or narrowed |
| NFKC + bidi/zero-width strip before the regex | `:297`–`306` | unchanged; `Stage1PipelineIT` @Order(4)/(5)/(6)/(14) unchanged |
| Stage 2 sees the pre-redaction original | `Stage1Result.originalBody` `:709`–`734` | unchanged — `originalBody` stays `normalized` |
| `stage1_flagged` true iff a rule matched | `:392`, `:427` | must become "either scan matched" |
| `quarantine.original_html` is the verbatim captured span | `V10__quarantine.sql:49` | never rewritten, including by remediation |

**The unit matters, not just the call** (§10): the second scan's unit is the
*whole final body*, the same unit the first scan uses. Do not narrow it to "the
part the transformation changed" — the synthesized line start in case (c) is
created by a boundary *between* two untouched runs.

## Verification strategy

| pitfall | catching test | input → asserted behavior |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | `Stage1PipelineIT.secondScanSharesTheSinglePerInputWatchdogAndMatchBudget`; `Stage1MatchOverflowIT` stays green | a body over the cap fails closed once, not twice |
| P2 | `Stage1PipelineIT.secondPassRedactionNeverOverwritesAFirstPassPlaceholder` | a first-pass hit inside a second-pass rule's `.{0,40}` window → each placeholder id still appears verbatim in the final body |
| P3 | `Stage1PipelineIT` @Order(8) plus a comment-rule case | `<<<UNTRUSTED>>>` and `<!-- … -->` still produce their quarantine rows |
| P4 | `Stage1BodyTextIT.plainTextPunctuationPersistsVerbatim`, `.urlQueryStringPersistsAsAWorkingUrl` | a markup-free body persists byte-identical; no whitespace collapse |
| P5 | `Stage1BodyTextIT.scriptAndStyleElementContentIsStillDropped` | `alert(1)` / `color:red` absent, body exactly `Visible` |
| P6 | `Stage1PipelineIT` @Order(12)/(13) via `SanitizerThrowingStage1Pipeline` | seam throw → `status='QUARANTINED'`, exactly one `sanitizer_exception` row |
| P7 | `Stage1BodyTextIT.redactionPlaceholderSurvivesByteExact` | marker byte-exact, exactly one occurrence |
| P8 | `Stage1PipelineIT.stage1ResultRedactedBodyEqualsTheStoredColumn` | `redactedBody()` equals the SELECTed column on a second-pass hit |
| P9 | `Stage1BodyTextIT.lineBreakSynthesizedByBlockCloseCannotHideAnImpersonationPrefix`, `.textRunsJoinedByInlineTagRemovalCannotHideADelimiterToken`, `.doublyEncodedDelimiterPayloadIsRedactedNotStoredLiteral`, `.normalizationSynthesizedEntityIsRedactedNotStoredLiteral` | payload redacted **and** a quarantine row exists with the expected `rule_id` |
| P10 | `Stage1PipelineIT.legitimatelyEscapedProseIsNotOverDecoded` | a body carrying `&amp;lt;` as prose still reads `&lt;`, never `<` |
| P11 | `Stage1BodyRemediationIT.remediationOutputMatchesTheLivePipelineForTheSameInput` | job output equals pipeline output for the same input |
| P12 | `Stage1BodyRemediationIT.savedPostSnapshotIsRemediated` | a corrupted snapshot with no surviving post row is remediated |
| P13 | `grep -rn "M1-776-2026-08-06" infochat-collector/src` | returns nothing |
| P14 | `Stage1BodyRemediationIT.aRemediatedRowIsNeverConvertedTwice` | a second run leaves a row whose text legitimately contains `<b>` untouched |

Failure-mode inputs are mandatory throughout and are already the majority of
the reproduction: every Group B case feeds hostile input whose whole point is
that the scan could not see it.

## Decomposition

Three tickets. Boundaries chosen so each is a single mechanism with its own
red test, and so no ticket both introduces a transformation and guards it.

1. **M1-785 — Stage 1 must scan the body text it stores.** Adds the second
   scan over the exact string about to be written, sharing one deadline and one
   match budget, with the placeholder-overlap rule. Touches
   `Stage1Pipeline.java` and adds methods to `Stage1PipelineIT`. Lands first;
   closes the live double-encoding bypass; changes no representation. Its
   reproduction is a NEW test (`Stage1PipelineIT`
   `.doublyEncodedEntityInjectionIsDetectedNotBypassed`) — none of the 11
   `Stage1BodyTextIT` cases goes green from this ticket alone, and the ticket
   says so. Pitfalls P1, P2, P3, P6, P8, P10.
2. **M1-784 — Stage 1 must store `post.body` as plain text.** Swaps the output
   sink; keeps the policy. Touches `Stage1Pipeline.java`, one new sink class,
   `docs/design/04-security.md` §4.2's rationale paragraph, and commits
   `Stage1BodyTextIT`. `blocked_by: [M1-785]` — with M1-785 in place, the two
   synthesis cases go green with no new scanning code. Pitfalls P4, P5, P6, P7,
   P9, P13.
3. **M1-786 — Remediate bodies stored before the fix.** `post.body` rows and
   `saved_post.body` snapshots, through the same conversion and the same scan
   (never a second decoder), gated at-most-once by a marker column.
   `blocked_by: [M1-784]`, `migration_touch: true`. Optional and deferrable:
   without it, the pipeline is correct for new posts while every already-stored
   body — and every permanent `/saved` snapshot — keeps its markup and
   entities. Pitfalls P7, P9, P11, P12, P14.

Sequencing is strict: 785 → 784 → 786. None may run in parallel — all three
touch the same Maven module and the second and third depend on the first's
invariant.

**Not filed, recorded here for the user:** `post.body_en`, `saved_post.body_en`
and `post.body_summary` are LLM-derived from the corrupted body. Re-deriving
them costs generative calls per row and is a separate decision; M1-786's Census
disposes of them explicitly rather than silently.

**Also not filed:** `post.title` is normalized (`PostPersister.java:187`) but
never HTML-stripped, so an RSS title containing markup keeps it. The evidence
file measured titles clean (`:95`), and no reproduction case covers it, so it
is named here and excluded from all three tickets rather than folded in.

## SPEC-GAP

None. `docs/spec/security.md §Ingest pipeline` is silent on the stored
representation and `docs/design/04-security.md §4.2` step 4 bullet 3 already
requires plain text; the second scan is a stricter reading of the same
section's "a prompt-injection regex set runs" against the same section's
placeholder-and-quarantine commitment. No promise is weakened, so no amendment
is owed.
